name: Smurfit Westrock plc
moat_justification: Real scale and vertical integration in a commodity product, but only about 6% of global containerboard capacity, limited demonstrated pricing power, cyclical volumes, and a capex bill that consumes most of operating cash flow — returns are earned by cost position and integration execution, not by a durable pricing moat.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 26.3%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 14.1x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Cyclical, capex-heavy packager with a weak-moderate moat 4/10 — does not clear 15% on any scenario at $41.28 (weighted IRR 6.96%, weighted IV@15 $14.54); it clears 15% only at ~$14.54, and the preliminary Tier B print was a merger basis-break artifact.
moat_for: Scale and vertical integration — mills feeding a large converting network across North America, EMEA/APAC and LATAM
Merger synergy and cost program — at least $400M synergy target plus footprint rationalization of WestRock assets
Diversified staple end-markets — food, beverage, consumer goods and e-commerce packaging demand
Sustainability positioning — paper packaging benefits from substitution away from plastic
moat_against: Commodity containerboard economics — about 6% global share, largely a price-taker; $100/ton hike is a test, not proof
Cyclical volumes and overcapacity — North America corrugated volumes fell in Q2 2026; new European capacity can blunt pricing
Capex intensity and leverage — TTM capex $2.282B vs OCF $3.297B; net debt $12.677B is 14.09x normalized OE
Input-cost exposure — higher 2026 freight and energy costs compress margins if pricing does not stick
